relationships.rationale: A sustained South China Sea crisis would increase the probability of sanctions, export controls, and retaliatory trade measures.
Maritime insecurity in the South China Sea can raise rerouting, insurance, delay, and freight-rate pressure.
A China–Japan crisis would increase the likelihood of coordinated economic restrictions and commercial retaliation.
Escalation affecting Japan and East China Sea logistics can disrupt semiconductor materials, equipment, and transport flows.
A sustained India–China border crisis would raise the probability of bilateral trade restrictions and technology controls.
Military escalation would intensify domestic political, fiscal, and security pressure in Pakistan.
Prolonged conflict could disrupt agriculture, trade, transport, and humanitarian access across vulnerable areas.
A blockade or coercive quarantine around Taiwan would immediately disrupt major container and transshipment routes.
A Taiwan blockade would trigger extensive sanctions, export controls, and retaliatory trade measures.
A Taiwan crisis would increase military activity and escalation risk across the northern South China Sea.
A prolonged semiconductor shortage would constrain industrial production and investment across major economies.
Strategic mineral restrictions would increase retaliatory trade and industrial-policy measures.
Export controls and retaliatory restrictions can materially constrain semiconductor equipment, inputs, and markets.
A major-power trade war would reduce trade, investment, productivity, and business confidence.
A major deterioration on the Ukrainian front increases the risk of incidents involving NATO territory, forces, or logistics.
Direct Russia–NATO escalation would increase the probability of gas infrastructure, transit, or supply disruption.
A material European gas supply shock would rapidly raise regional and global energy prices.
A prolonged European gas shock would weaken industrial output, household demand, and regional growth.
Escalation near South Caucasus energy corridors can increase regional supply-risk premiums.
A Serbia–Kosovo crisis can intensify nationalist mobilization and protest activity in the region.
Regional military escalation involving Iran materially increases closure, interdiction, mining, or attack risk in Hormuz.
Regional escalation can increase proxy attacks and maritime threats affecting Red Sea shipping.
Sustained Iran–Israel escalation raises energy supply-risk premiums and physical-disruption risk.
Severe disruption of Hormuz would directly constrain oil and LNG flows.
A prolonged Hormuz disruption would pressure energy-importing currencies and reserves.
Sustained Red Sea insecurity can reduce traffic and create operational disruption affecting the Suez corridor.
Sustained Red Sea disruption would increase rerouting, freight rates, and container imbalances.
Material Suez throughput disruption would immediately affect global container schedules and capacity.
Higher energy, fertilizer, transport, storage, and production costs transmit into food-security risk.
Higher import costs would intensify external financing and currency pressure in vulnerable economies.
A sustained Panama Canal capacity reduction would increase rerouting, delays, and freight costs.
A major disruption in the Strait of Malacca would affect a critical share of Asia-linked maritime trade.
Malacca disruption would constrain energy transit and increase delivery-risk premiums.
Closure of a major port can create vessel queues, schedule disruption, and container imbalances.
A sustained global shipping shock would raise trade costs and weaken industrial and consumer activity.
A material attack on payment, clearing, or banking infrastructure would immediately create liquidity and confidence stress.
A coordinated infrastructure campaign can include or exploit undersea communications disruptions.
Major cable disruption can degrade financial connectivity and magnify concurrent cyber incidents.
Severe communications disruption can impair port, logistics, and maritime coordination systems.
Sustained GNSS disruption can impair navigation, port approaches, aviation, and logistics coordination.
Regional GNSS interference can reduce safe port access and throughput.
AI-enabled influence operations increase the scale, speed, and plausibility of election interference.
Coordinated synthetic media and narratives can accelerate mobilization and public disorder.
Material disruption of electoral confidence can increase protest and unrest risk.
Severe China financial stress can transmit through banks, markets, property exposure, and confidence.
A deep China slowdown would weaken global demand, trade, commodities, and investment.
Broad banking stress would tighten credit and materially weaken investment and demand.
Global banking stress would tighten external financing for vulnerable sovereigns.
Acute depreciation and reserve loss directly worsen foreign-currency debt sustainability.
Sovereign debt distress can constrain food imports, subsidies, and humanitarian spending.
Escalating cross-border militancy would increase domestic security and political pressure in Pakistan.
Severe instability can increase crisis miscalculation, militant activity, or diversionary escalation risk.
A broader coup wave can reduce deterrence and increase unconstitutional-transfer risk in the Sahel.
Regime failure and insecurity can accelerate protest, repression, and political mobilization.
Large-scale protest escalation can intensify institutional paralysis in Bangladesh.
Large protest movements can compound governance and security pressure in Nigeria.
State fragmentation would worsen displacement, market access, agriculture, and humanitarian delivery.
State collapse in Haiti would intensify import, distribution, and humanitarian-access constraints.
Major instability in Nigeria can add regional grain and food-market pressure.
Regional spillover from Sudan would worsen displacement, market disruption, and humanitarian access.
Regional militarization and border pressure can increase Ethiopia–Eritrea escalation risk.
Renewed conflict would disrupt agriculture, trade, displacement routes, and humanitarian access.
Regional conflict in eastern DRC can constrain production and transport of strategic minerals.
Expanded conflict would intensify displacement and food insecurity in affected areas.
Escalation near offshore energy assets can increase localized supply-risk premiums.
Concurrent drought across major producing regions would materially reduce grain output and export availability.
Persistent drought directly intensifies water availability and allocation stress.
Severe water scarcity constrains agriculture, livestock, household supply, and food affordability.
A global grain shock would directly reduce food availability and raise prices in import-dependent states.
Acute food-price and availability deterioration can increase protest and political-instability risk.
A severe cross-border outbreak can weaken labor supply, mobility, confidence, and economic activity.
A cross-border health emergency can disrupt labor, logistics, markets, and humanitarian operations.
